mainTopic: How the ציצית/כלאים pairing is learned from סמוכים, and why the words 'צמר ופשתים' are extra yet still teach that wool and linen may be crossed in ציצית
overview: The גמרא is explaining when רבי יהודה learns laws from verses placed side by side (סמוכים). He does this only when the link is obvious (מוכח) or a verse is extra (מופנה). The ציצית verse placed next to the כלאים verse qualifies for one of these two reasons. The גמרא first shows that both כלאים verses, 'לא יעלה עליך' and 'לא תלבש שעטנז', are needed, since each fixes a gap in the other. It then finds that the words 'צמר ופשתים' are extra, because the school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that every 'garment' in the תורה means wool or linen, and a word-link of 'שעטנז / שעטנז' covers the rest. Next the גמרא asks why these extra words are needed to allow כלאים in ציצית at all. The תורה already requires a wool תכלת thread, even on linen garments. The answer is that without 'צמר ופשתים' we might read 'הכנף' to mean the threads must match the garment's material. That reading would forbid wool threads on linen and linen threads on wool, and 'צמר ופשתים' teaches that this crossing is allowed.

steps.title: Conclusion: the extra verse is free to teach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up its earlier argument: since a verse was not needed for its plain meaning, it is free to teach something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the verse is free to teach an additional law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the argument it was making just before this. It concludes that the verse it was discussing is extra, so it is 'free' to teach a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the earlier proof that רבי יהודה does learn from סמוכים in ספר דברים when a verse is מופנה. A verse that looks repeated must be there to teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this

phrases.english: Learn from this that it is free [to teach].
phrases.notes: This finishes the point just before this, about a verse that seemed repeated and so is free for a new lesson.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument that began before this section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The earlier verse is מופנה, so רבי יהודה may learn from its placement.

steps.title: The ציצית case also qualifies, for one of two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ציצית/כלאים pairing also meets רבי יהודה's standard, either because the lesson is obvious or because the verse is extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding ציצית as well, there is a reason to learn from the placement. If you want, say it is because it is obvious. If you want, say it is because the verse is free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now applies the rule to the ציצית/כלאים case and gives two possible reasons it qualifies. This line sets up the next two steps, which explain each reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה only learns from verses placed side by side when there is a special signal. The גמרא offers two different signals for ציצית: מוכח (the placement clearly means something) or מופנה (a verse is extra).

keyTerms.meaning: Fringes on a four-cornered garment
If you want, say; it introduces one of two possible answers
Obvious or evident from the context

phrases.english: And regarding ציצית as well,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same standard (מוכח or מופנה) to the ציצית/כלאים pairing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציצית/כלאים pairing qualifies for רבי יהודה's דרשה, either as מוכח or as מופנה.

steps.title: First reason: the placement is obviously meaningful
steps.stepSummary: If the verse were not meant to be connected to כלאים, the תורה would have placed it with the main ציצית section. Its placement here must be on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because it is obvious. If it were not meant to teach something, the תורה should have written it in the ציצית section. For what law did it write it here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'obvious' reason. The ציצית verse is out of its natural place, so its location next to כלאים must be teaching something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ציצית already has its own section in the תורה. Repeating ציצית here, right next to שעטנז, only makes sense if the two are meant to be linked. That link is that כלאים is allowed in ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One; a name for the תורה or ה׳ as the Author
The ציצית section of the תורה
For what law? Why is it needed?

phrases.english: If you want, say it is because it is obvious —

by the ציצית section,
for what law did it write it here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two reasons given in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the ציצית/כלאים pairing is מוכח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ציצית verse is placed away from its own section, so its location must be intentional.

steps.title: Second reason: the שעטנז verse is extra
steps.stepSummary: The תורה already forbade כלאים clothing in ויקרא, so the repeat in דברים looks extra and is free to teach the ציצית lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because it is free. After all, the תורה already wrote: 'A garment of mixed kinds, שעטנז, shall not come upon you.' Why do I need 'Do not wear שעטנז'? Learn from this that it is free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'free' reason. The ban on כלאים clothing appears twice, so the second time must be there to teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the signal is not the placement of the ציצית verse but the repeated שעטנז verse. If 'לא תלבש שעטנז' adds nothing to the ויקרא verse, it is מופנה and can be used for the סמוכים lesson.

steps.title: Both verses are needed: 'לא יעלה' alone would be too broad
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the 'free' reason. With only 'לא יעלה עליך,' we would forbid even clothing sellers who drape garments on themselves. 'לא תלבש' limits the ban to wearing that gives הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These verses are both needed. If the תורה wrote only 'shall not come upon you,' I would think it forbids any way of putting it on, even for clothing sellers. So it wrote 'Do not wear שעטנז': like wearing, which gives benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim in step 4 that 'לא תלבש שעטנז' is extra. It starts showing that each verse teaches its own point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא יעלה' alone sounds like anything placed on you is forbidden, even a seller carrying garments on his shoulders. 'לא תלבש' narrows it to cases like real wearing, which gives הנאה. So 'לא תלבש' is not extra.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'לא תלבש' is needed to limit 'לא יעלה' to beneficial wearing, so it is not extra.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches the practical law that carrying כלאים garments without wearing them for benefit, as sellers do, is not forbidden.

steps.title: And 'לא תלבש' alone would be too narrow
steps.stepSummary: With only 'לא תלבש,' we would forbid only real wearing and allow simply placing a garment on oneself. So 'לא יעלה עליך' is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה wrote only 'Do not wear,' I would say only wearing is forbidden, since it gives a lot of benefit. But placing it on yourself would be allowed. So it wrote 'shall not come upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes showing that both verses are needed. Here it explains what 'לא יעלה עליך' adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא תלבש' alone could be read as covering only full wearing, which gives warmth and looks nice. 'לא יעלה' extends the ban to draping a garment on yourself for benefit, such as warmth. Each verse fills a gap in the other, so neither is extra.

steps.whatToRemember: Each כלאים verse is needed. 'לא יעלה' alone would forbid too much (even sellers), and 'לא תלבש' alone would forbid too little (only full wearing). So the 'free verse' reason for the ציצית lesson is pushed back.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'לא יעלה' is needed to include draping a garment on oneself for benefit.

steps.title: Even so, why write 'wool and linen'?
steps.stepSummary: Even granting that both verbs are needed, the תורה could have written just 'לא תלבש שעטנז.' The words 'צמר ופשתים' look extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should have written only 'Do not wear שעטנז.' Why do I need the words 'wool and linen'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the last answer but points to another part of the verse that still seems extra. It sets up the next step, which shows why those words are extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5–6 showed that 'לא תלבש' is not wasted. But the full verse in דברים also says 'צמר ופשתים.' If that phrase teaches nothing new, it is extra and free to teach the ציצית lesson.

phrases.english: If so, let the Merciful One write

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from steps 5–6 that the verse in דברים has no extra words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if both verbs are needed, the words 'צמר ופשתים' still seem to add nothing

steps.title: We already know clothing means wool and linen
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that 'clothing' in the תורה always means wool and linen. So writing 'צמר ופשתים' in דברים is extra and is free for the ציצית lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, the תורה already wrote: 'A garment of כלאים שעטנז shall not come upon you.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: since the תורה says 'garments' without describing them, and in one place it spelled out wool and linen, all garments mean wool and linen. So why did the תורה write 'wool and linen' here? Learn from this that it is free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the words 'צמר ופשתים' are extra, since we already know that 'garment' means wool and linen. So these words are free to teach the ציצית lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא only says 'בגד' with no materials named. The school of רבי ישמעאל uses the laws of צרעת on clothing, where the תורה names wool and linen, to show that every 'garment' in the תורה means wool and linen. So the כלאים ban is already limited to wool and linen, and saying it again in דברים is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

steps.title: Maybe wearing would ban every mixture
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: without 'צמר ופשתים' we might think 'לא תלבש,' which gives more pleasure, forbids any two kinds of fabric, not just wool and linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still needed. You might have thought: placing a garment on yourself gives little benefit, so only wool and linen is forbidden. But actually wearing it gives great benefit, so maybe the תורה forbade any two kinds together. So the תורה wrote 'wool and linen.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues that 'צמר ופשתים' is not extra after all. It may be needed to limit the wearing ban to wool and linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of רבי ישמעאל's school might only cover 'לא יעלה עליך' (placing), which is a lighter benefit. For real wearing, which gives more benefit, we might have thought any mixture is forbidden. The words 'צמר ופשתים' would then be needed to block that.

steps.title: A word-link would teach it anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the verse could have left out 'צמר ופשתים' and learned it from the word 'שעטנז,' which appears in both verses. So the words are still extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse should have said nothing about it, and we would learn it from 'שעטנז' here and 'שעטנז' in the verse about placing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback and shows that 'צמר ופשתים' really is extra after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses use the word 'שעטנז.' Through this word-link (גזירה שוה), the wearing ban would also be limited to wool and linen, just like the placing ban. Since the תורה wrote 'צמר ופשתים' anyway, the words are extra and free to teach the ציצית lesson.

steps.whatToRemember: 'צמר ופשתים' in דברים is extra: we already know garments mean wool and linen, and for wearing we could learn it from 'שעטנז / שעטנז.' So it is free to link ציצית with כלאים.

steps.title: Why would we ever think כלאים is forbidden in ציצית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that without 'צמר ופשתים' we would forbid כלאים in ציצית. The תורה already commands ציצית on garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the school of רבי ישמעאל, we only allow כלאים in ציצית because the תורה wrote 'wool and linen.' Does that mean that without those words we would forbid it? But the פסוק says to make ציצית on the corners of garments!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the whole idea that the extra words 'צמר ופשתים' are needed to permit כלאים in ציצית. The proof for this challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps said 'צמר ופשתים' is extra and is used to teach that כלאים is allowed in ציצית. Here the גמרא asks why we would need that teaching at all. The פסוק about ציצית on 'garments' may already show that כלאים is allowed.

steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: all 'garments' in the תורה are wool or linen. The תורה says to put תכלת on them, and תכלת is wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its challenge. A linen garment needs a wool תכלת thread, so the תורה itself commands כלאים in ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put the pieces together. 'Garments' includes linen ones, and every garment gets תכלת. Since תכלת is wool, a linen garment with ציצית has wool and linen together, so no extra words should be needed to permit it.

steps.title: Since שש is linen, תכלת is wool
steps.stepSummary: The תורה calls linen by a special name, 'שש.' So the other materials listed with it, including תכלת, must be wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since 'שש' is linen, תכלת must be wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that תכלת is wool. When the תורה lists materials, linen gets its own name, 'שש,' so תכלת must be something else: wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה names linen separately as 'שש,' then the colored threads listed next to it are not linen. That leaves wool, and so the proof in step 12 holds.

steps.title: The words are needed because of רבא's reasoning

steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra words, we might read 'הכנף' to mean that ציצית must be the same material as the garment. steps.title: רבא's contradiction between 'הכנף' and 'צמר ופשתים'
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out two verses that seem to clash. 'הכנף' suggests the threads must match the corner, while 'צמר ופשתים' suggests the threads must be wool or linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised a contradiction. It says 'הכנף,' meaning the same kind as the corner, and it also says 'wool and linen'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's contradiction between two verses. His resolution comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הכנף' suggests the ציצית must be the same material as the garment's corner. 'צמר ופשתים' (placed right next to the ציצית verses) suggests ציצית should be wool or linen. Both cannot be true in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a contradiction
The same kind as the corner

phrases.english: As Rava raised a contradiction:
It is written "the corner," meaning the same kind as the corner,
and it is written "wool and linen"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of רבא that step 15 mentioned.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule for what material ציצית threads must be
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'הכנף' requires the threads to match the garment, while 'צמר ופשתים' points to wool or linen regardless of the garment.

steps.title: Wool and linen work on any garment; other materials only on their own kind
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the clash. Wool and linen threads work on any garment, while other materials work only on a garment of the same material.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Wool and linen work both on their own kind and not on their own kind. Other materials work on their own kind, but not on a different kind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles his contradiction. Each verse covers a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צמר ופשתים' tells us wool and linen threads are good on any garment. 'הכנף' (same as the corner) applies only to other materials like silk. This is why the extra words matter: without them, a wool thread on a linen garment would not count.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (how do we fit both together)
Exempt, meaning they fulfill the obligation
Of their own kind (same material as the garment)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: wool and linen threads work on any garment, while other materials work only on their own kind. Step 15 used this rule to explain why 'צמר ופשתים' is needed, but step 18 challenges whether the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל can rely on it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'פוטרין' here does not mean the garment is free from ציצית. It means these threads are valid, so the garment's obligation is fulfilled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets רבא's practical rule for which threads can be used on garments of different materials. The גמרא will soon ask whether the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל can use this rule at all (step 18).

phrases.english: How so?
Wool and linen threads fulfill the obligation
whether on their own kind or not on their own kind.
Other kinds of material, on their own kind, fulfill the obligation,
but not on their own kind, they do not fulfill it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבא's contradiction from step 16, which completes the answer of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: each verse covers a different kind of material
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הכנף' might require matching material for every kind of thread.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wool and linen threads work on any garment. Other materials must match the garment.

steps.title: But the school of רבי ישמעאל does not hold like רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל does not hold like רבא. So רבא's reasoning cannot explain why this תנא needs 'צמר ופשתים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא from the school of רבי ישמעאל does not hold like רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 15. That answer said 'צמר ופשתים' was needed so we would not reason like רבא. But this תנא does not accept רבא's view in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reasoning matters only if garments made of other materials also need ציצית. The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל holds that only wool and linen garments need ציצית. So for him, רבא's distinction never comes up, and the reason given in Step 15 does not work for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
He does not hold of (this view)

phrases.english: But the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael
does not hold of Rava's view!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from Step 15, which relied on רבא's reasoning from Steps 16-17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 15 that the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל needs 'צמר ופשתים' because of רבא's reasoning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's reasoning assumes that garments of other materials need ציצית. This תנא rejects that, so the reasoning cannot explain why he needs the words.

steps.title: The words are needed to allow wool on linen and linen on wool
steps.stepSummary: Even without רבא's view, we might have read 'הכנף' as 'same material as the corner': wool for wool and linen for linen, with תכלת only on wool. 'צמר ופשתים' teaches that mixing them also works.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is still necessary. You might have thought, following a reading like רבא's, that 'הכנף' means 'the same kind as the corner.' Then the תורה would be saying: make wool threads for a wool garment and linen threads for a linen garment. And when you make wool for wool, dye it with תכלת. But wool for linen, or linen for wool, would not be allowed. So the תורה wrote 'צמר ופשתים' to teach that even wool for linen and linen for wool is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 15. It shows another wrong reading of 'הכנף' that this תנא could have fallen into, and 'צמר ופשתים' is needed to block it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea uses the same reading as רבא, that 'הכנף' means 'the same kind as the corner.' But here it is applied only to wool and linen: the threads would have to match the garment exactly. 'צמר ופשתים' tells us that wool and linen can be crossed, so a wool garment can take linen threads and a linen garment can take wool threads.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (the verse is still needed)
It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
An inference drawn from the exact wording
The same kind (of material) as the corner
Dye it (include the dyed תכלת thread)

steps.whatToRemember: Even for the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, 'צמר ופשתים' is needed. It teaches that wool threads may go on a linen garment and linen threads on a wool garment, not only matching material.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not רבא's actual rule. רבא allowed wool and linen on anything. This step describes a different, mistaken reading of 'הכנף' that the words 'צמר ופשתים' come to reject.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the answer of Step 15. Even for the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, who does not hold like רבא, the words 'צמר ופשתים' have a real job for ציצית, so the challenge of Steps 11-12 is answered.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for it would enter your mind to say,
like the inference of Rava:
"The corner" means the same kind as the corner,
and this is what the Merciful One is saying:
make for it wool threads for a wool garment
and linen threads for a linen garment.
And when you make wool for wool, dye it;
phrases.notes: 'Dye it' means put in the blue תכלת thread.

phrases.english: but wool for linen
or linen for wool would not be allowed.
So the Merciful One wrote "wool and linen,"
to teach that even wool for linen
and linen for wool are fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא, כִּי דִיּוּקָא דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 18 by giving a different reason why 'צמר ופשתים' is needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the verse has another needed job that does not depend on רבא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הכנף' means the threads must match the garment exactly, wool for wool and linen for linen, with תכלת only when wool is on wool. Mixing would not be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'צמר ופשתים' teaches that wool threads on a linen garment and linen threads on a wool garment are valid.
